title: My technology habits
writingModel:
My Technology Habits — An Honest Assessment
By Kamila Seitkali, WKU, Group A1.1

Technology is the central tool of my daily life as a university student. I use my phone, laptop, and tablet constantly — for studying, communicating, and entertainment. In this essay, I want to describe my current technology habits honestly, identify the positive and negative aspects, and explain what I plan to change.

My daily routine starts digitally. I always check my messages as soon as I wake up — WhatsApp for family, Telegram for university group chats, and a quick glance at Instagram. I usually spend about twenty minutes on my phone before I even have breakfast. During lectures, I always use Google Docs to take notes, which I find much more efficient than paper. I often record short audio clips on my phone when the lecturer speaks too quickly to type.

For studying, technology has completely transformed how I learn. I need to study vocabulary every day because English requires constant revision, so I use the Anki app for fifteen minutes every morning. I also enjoy watching YouTube videos in English — it helps me improve my listening skills while learning interesting content. I sometimes use ChatGPT to check my English writing before I submit it. I plan to use it less as my skills improve, because I want to develop independence.

However, I also have some bad habits that I need to change. My biggest problem is social media. I check Instagram about thirty times a day, which I know is too much. I also avoid using my phone in "no phone" zones at the library, but I forget to do it consistently. My screen time app tells me I spend an average of three hours and forty minutes per day on my phone — much more than I realised. This affects my concentration during study sessions, which I find very frustrating.

I have made a list of changes I want to make. First, I plan to turn off all Instagram notifications so that I only check it intentionally, at a time I choose. Second, I need to stop using my phone in bed — I want to read a physical book for thirty minutes before sleeping instead. Third, I hope to reduce my daily screen time to under two hours by the end of this semester. I know these changes will not be easy, but I believe they are worth making.

To conclude: technology is neither good nor bad — it depends on how we use it. I enjoy using my laptop and apps for learning and staying connected. But I need to use social media more intentionally. I want to control technology; I never want to let it control me. Starting this week — not next Monday this time! 😊
